column3: “Knowledge of wind” is rendered “windy knowledge,” and “his belly” as “himself.”
“Your iniquity teaches your mouth” is rendered “your guilt teaches your mouth,” and “tongue” as “language.”
“The council of God” is rendered “the secret counsel of God.”
“Old more than your father, days” is rendered “Older than your father.”
“Watched for the sword” is rendered “destined for the sword.”
NASB supplies “saying,” and “prepared in his hand” is rendered “at hand.” The ancient Greek reads differently, and the meaning is uncertain.
“Anxiety and distress” is rendered “Distress and anguish,” and “battle” as “attack.”
“With the thickness of the bosses of his shields” is rendered “With his massive shield.”
“Made fat on loins” is rendered “made his thighs heavy with flesh.”
“Their property” is rendered “his grain”; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
NASB capitalizes “His mouth,” taking it as God's; the Hebrew may refer to the flame.
